description: Null unless the payload states a threshold under `## Tests to write` and this verdict establishes the candidate at or above it, judged on the severity it settles on, revision included. Then: the failing test written in the disposable copy, the command that runs it and what that run printed. A test the engine cannot accept is set aside with the reason and the verdict stands.

files.description: Every file written for this test, relative to the copy's root: the test file, and any fixture it needs. Never a file under review, never under `.git`, never with `..`.

argv.description: The command that runs this one test, first element the program. Given for `written_not_run` too: the command that would run it.

cwd.description: Working directory for `argv`, relative to the root of the copy; `.` for the root.

exit_status.description: The exit status of the run: non-zero for `red`; null for `written_not_run`, where nothing ran.

output.description: Captured stdout and stderr of the run, bounded as evidence output is; the tail is kept when cut. Empty for `written_not_run`.

truncated.description: Whether `output` was cut to the bound.

state.description: red = it ran and failed by assertion, for the stated reason; written_not_run = no run was possible here. A test that passed, or failed at an import or a typo, is neither: it is not reported.

fails_because.description: One sentence for a person: the assertion that fails and why that is the defect.

expected_failure.description: The exact text the failing run prints that shows the defect, such as the assertion message, copied from `output`; the engine looks for it there. Required for `red`; for `written_not_run`, what the owner should see, or null.
